For example, a protein-protein interaction layer, a co-expression layer, and a genetic interaction layer can be combined so that cross-layer algorithms (PageRank, community detection) integrate information from all three. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [layers]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary mapping layer names to `Graph` objects. Every graph must contain exactly the same set of node labels. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `layers` is empty or if the node-label sets of the graphs differ. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#0cca56ef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ppi = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) coex = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") ) mpx = ec.MultiplexGraph({"ppi": ppi, "coex": coex}) mpx ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` MultiplexGraph(3 nodes, layers=[ppi(1 edges), coex(1 edges)]) ``` ::: ::: ##
